Subject: Subprocessor addition request & Order Form amendment needed

Hi Neha —

Quick heads up: we need to add a subprocessor (Kubico Labs) to the stack for the new ingestion pipeline in our DataStream product. Kubico will handle log normalization + short-term blob storage for dedup. This change pushes our monthly token throughput above the committed tier from the existing order form, so we also need an Order Form amendment for billing and an explicit subprocessor flow-down in the DPA.

What we can provide now:
- Kubico SAAS overview (attached)
- Proposed scope spreadsheet with exact services and retention windows (attached)
- Kubico says they have SOC 2 Type II and a short security attestation PDF they can share

What we need from Redwood:
1) Confirmation that Kubico can be added under your current MSA/DPA flowdown (or a list of required flowdown clauses).
2) A suggested Order Form amendment so procurement can process the capacity uplift quickly.
3) Any additional evidence you need from Kubico (SOC 2 cert, encryption detail, KMS usage, right-to-audit language).

Target: get legal signoff + order form amendment in next 10 business days so we can onboard before the end of April.

Thanks — appreciate the quick triage.

Alice Moreno
Head of Platform Partnerships
DataWave Analytics

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com

Date: Wed, 2 Apr 2025 13:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor addition request & Order Form amendment needed

Neha / team —

Thanks for the ping and attachments. I reviewed Kubico's overview and the requested scope. High-level legal guidance and required flowdown items below. I attached a starter DPA addendum redline for procurement to use as a baseline.

Required flowdown clauses we must get into Kubico's subproc agreement (minimum):
- Security controls: must map to our DPA Appendix A controls (encryption in transit + at rest, MFA for operator access, vulnerability patch SLAs).
- SOC 2 Type II: provide latest report and scope; we need to validate no carve-outs for services they will perform.
- Right to audit: Redwood or our auditor must have the ability to audit Kubico where they process Redwood customer data; 30 days' notice ok, scope limited to relevant systems.
- Breach notification: 24 hours initial notification to Redwood's security lead + 72 hours full report, plus cooperation obligations.
- Sub-subprocessors: Kubico must provide a list and 30-day notice before onboarding any new sub-subprocessor that will access customer data.
- Data residency & transfers: specify permitted regions; if Kubico will store EU data, ensure adequate safeguards (SCCs or equivalent).
- Data return & deletion: upon termination, Kubico must return or securely delete data within 30 days and provide verification.
- Indemnity/LI limitation: we cannot accept open-ended carveouts. Any limitations to liability must be reasonable and tied to the services.

Open questions / items for procurement to capture in the Order Form amendment:
- Exact monthly unit increase and effective date (procurement).
- Whether Kubico requires any inbound credentials or long-lived keys (security).
- If Kubico insists on a specific liability carveout, escalate to the executive exceptions process.

Timing: I can produce a DPA addendum draft by EOD tomorrow. If Kubico provides SOC 2 and the attestation PDF (as Alice mentioned), we can move to signature after procurement finalizes the order form figures.

Attaching: DPA_subproc_addendum_draft.docx (draft redline).

-Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
From: Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@datwave.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: legal@kubicolabs.com
Date: Thu, 3 Apr 2025 09:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor addition request & Order Form amendment needed

Thanks — appreciate the fast turnaround, Kimberly.

Quick answers from Kubico:
- SOC 2 Type II report attached (Kubico_Security_Attestation.pdf). They confirmed the report covers the log processing and storage services in scope (no carve-outs for the relevant modules).
- Kubico can accept our standard flowdown language with one requested exception: they want an explicit cap on consequential damages for subprocessor liability tied to their contract with us. They say their customers require this and it is standard for them.
- Kubico does not store EU personal data for this engagement; all processing will be in us-west and us-east.

Next steps from our side: procurement can provide the estimated volumetric uplift today and we'll sign the Order Form amendment once Redwood confirms the DPA addendum language.

If Redwood is ok with the liability cap (we understand legal may want to escalate), let us know and we can prepare a final redline for execution.

Alice Moreno
Head of Platform Partnerships
DataWave Analytics
alice.moreno@datwave.com
Attachments: Kubico_Security_Attestation.pdf
